panels.title: Events over time (by type)
panels.description: analytics.behavioral_events, bucketed by time. Uses COALESCE(occurred_at, received_at): synthetic seed data only sets occurred_at (spread over the last 60 days), live events only set received_at (the moment the API ingested them) — see app/analytics/models.py and app/api/analytics_client.py. The COALESCE is computed in a subquery, not passed directly to $__timeGroup/$__timeFilter — those macros' argument parsing breaks on a comma inside nested parens.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroup(event_time, '$__interval') AS "time",
  event_type AS "metric",
  count(*) AS "value"
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(occurred_at, received_at) AS event_time, event_type
  FROM analytics.behavioral_events
) e
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Recommendation -> click -> apply/save funnel
panels.description: Total event counts by type across the selected time range — read top to bottom as the funnel: recommendation_shown -> recommendation_clicked -> job_applied/job_saved.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_type, count(*) AS events
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(occurred_at, received_at) AS event_time, event_type
  FROM analytics.behavioral_events
) e
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
GROUP BY event_type
ORDER BY events DESC

SELECT
  CASE WHEN sum((event_type = 'recommendation_shown')::int) = 0 THEN 0
  ELSE 100.0 * sum((event_type = 'recommendation_clicked')::int) / sum((event_type = 'recommendation_shown')::int)
  END AS click_through_rate
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(occurred_at, received_at) AS event_time, event_type
  FROM analytics.behavioral_events
) e
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)

SELECT
  CASE WHEN sum((event_type = 'recommendation_clicked')::int) = 0 THEN 0
  ELSE 100.0 * sum((event_type = 'job_applied')::int) / sum((event_type = 'recommendation_clicked')::int)
  END AS apply_rate
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(occurred_at, received_at) AS event_time, event_type
  FROM analytics.behavioral_events
) e
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)

SELECT actor_type, count(DISTINCT actor_id) AS distinct_actors
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(occurred_at, received_at) AS event_time, actor_type, actor_id
  FROM analytics.behavioral_events
) e
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
GROUP BY actor_type
ORDER BY actor_type

panels.title: Active users per day (by actor type)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroup(event_time, '1d') AS "time",
  actor_type AS "metric",
  count(DISTINCT actor_id) AS "value"
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(occurred_at, received_at) AS event_time, actor_type, actor_id
  FROM analytics.behavioral_events
) e
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Recent activity (raw events)
panels.description: The "what did user X just do" view — most recent behavioral_events rows first.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(occurred_at, received_at) AS time,
  actor_type,
  actor_id,
  event_type,
  entity_type,
  entity_id,
  source,
  session_id
FROM analytics.behavioral_events
ORDER BY COALESCE(occurred_at, received_at) DESC
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Recent edits (audit trail)
panels.description: entity_change_log — who changed which field on a candidate_details/job_details record, old -> new, and when. See app/audit/.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  changed_at AS time,
  entity_type,
  entity_id,
  changed_by_keycloak_user_id AS changed_by,
  changes::text AS changes
FROM entity_change_log
ORDER BY changed_at DESC
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Extraction calls needing human review, per day
panels.description: extraction_calls.needs_review, bucketed by called_at. document_confidence is a heuristic proxy (no ground truth exists for real production text) — see app/extraction/pipeline.py:_document_confidence for the formula and the golden-eval validation behind the 0.6 cutoff. Watch this for sudden spikes: a jump usually means a model/prompt/threshold change regressed quality, not that the underlying text got harder overnight.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroup(called_at, '1d') AS "time",
  CASE WHEN needs_review THEN 'needs_review' ELSE 'ok' END AS "metric",
  count(*) AS "value"
FROM extraction_calls
WHERE $__timeFilter(called_at)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Open review backlog (flagged, not yet reviewed)
panels.description: A human hasn't closed these out yet — this is the number that should trend toward zero, not the daily-flagged count above (which will never be zero on a healthy pipeline, since some fraction of real text is always genuinely ambiguous).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS open_backlog
FROM extraction_calls
WHERE needs_review AND reviewed_at IS NULL

SELECT avg(document_confidence) AS avg_confidence
FROM extraction_calls
WHERE called_at >= now() - interval '7 days'

panels.title: Review queue — flagged documents awaiting a human (link to MLflow trace)
panels.description: mlflow_trace_id is the jump-off point into that exact extraction's full per-phrase trace in the MLflow UI (http://localhost:5000 locally) — paste it into MLflow's trace search, or use the Data link below once MLFLOW_BASE_URL is set to this environment's real MLflow host. Same split of responsibility as the panels above: this dashboard says how many and which ones, MLflow says why.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  called_at AS time,
  llm_model,
  text_length,
  match_count,
  unmatched_count,
  document_confidence,
  mlflow_trace_id
FROM extraction_calls
WHERE needs_review AND reviewed_at IS NULL
ORDER BY called_at DESC
LIMIT 200
